approach: Write the position of each particle as a function of time and solve for the time at which the two positions are equal.

steps.text: Write the position of particle 1, starting at x = −10 m with velocity −4 m/s and acceleration +2 m/s².
Write the position of particle 2, starting at x = +2 m with velocity +6 m/s and acceleration −2 m/s².
Set the two positions equal and solve the resulting quadratic for t, keeping the positive root.
Substitute t = 6 s into either position equation to get the collision point.

common_mistakes.text: Taking t = −1 s, the other root of the quadratic, as the collision time, which is not physical since time cannot be negative.
Writing particle 1's acceleration term as −t² instead of +t² by keeping the sign of its velocity for the acceleration too, which changes the quadratic and its root.
